sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cairenn, also Caireann, was the secondary wife of King Eochaid Mugmedón. She was a captured slave from Britain. Her son was Niall of the Nine Hostages. Niall's line became the Uí Néill dynasty. MacKillop gives her the title Cairenn Chasdub, which means of the dark curly hair. She was the daughter of Sachall Balb of the Britons. Eochaid's queen Mongfhind hated Cairenn. Mongfhind forced Cairenn to draw household water during her pregnancy. Cairenn worked until she gave birth to Niall. Her son became a high king of Tara.

okr.objective: An Irish heroine whose son carried the royal line of Tara.
key_results: Cairenn, a captured British slave, became the secondary wife of King Eochaid Mugmedón.
She bore Niall of the Nine Hostages, ancestor of the Uí Néill dynasty.
Queen Mongfhind forced her to draw water until she delivered Niall.
Cairenn's son became a high king of Tara.
